newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, AGAs seen neutral.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, AGAs seen neutral.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended higher across the board Wednesday in a moderate session, then showed little movement on ACCESS after a weekly AGA stock build that fell within expectations, market sources said.

Earlier, June climbed 1.5 cents to close at $2.206 per million British thermal units, then sold at $2.205 in after-hours trade following the report. July settled 1.7 cents higher at $2.247. Other deferreds ended up by two to 5.7 cents.
"The number is neutral. It's perfect for a market that has done nothing recently," said Chris Bray at United Fuels, noting prices have been stuck in the same range for two weeks.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 62 bcf, in line with an earlier Reuters poll for a 55-65 bcf build. Overall stocks are still 219 bcf, or 27 percent, above year-ago levels. Eastern storage, which gained 36 bcf last week, remained 119 bcf, or 34 percent, over 1996 levels.

Most agreed there was little reason to break out of the recent range, but with better summer air conditioning demand just around the corner, some saw the scales tilted slightly in favor of the bulls now.

Technical traders still pegged June support and resistance at $2.15 and $2.30, respectively. Major buying should emerge at the $2.05 double bottom, with good selling likely at the $2.43 contract high.

In the cash, Gulf Coast swing prices Wednesday were steady to down slightly in the high-teens. Midcon pipes were little changed at about $2.00. New York city gate gas also held relatively steady in the mid-$2.40s.
Maintenance on Transco's Texas line will continue to cut about 400 mmcfd out of a total capacity of about 600 mmcfd through Thursday.

Planned work on Mobil's Mary Ann gas processing plant in Coden, Ala., has cut the plant's total processing capacity of 380-390 mmcfd. About 120 mmcfd should be back within the next seven days, with the balance due back in three weeks.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip rose 2.1 cents to $2.272. NYMEX said 37,872 contracts traded, down from Tuesday's revised tally of 57,023.

On the KCBT, June finished 2.5 cents higher at $2.07, while deferreds ended up by one to 2.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.9 cent to 13.6 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 286 lots traded, down from Tuesday's total of 532.
